body:
### Environment

Node version: v24.14.1
npm version: 11.11.1
Local ESLint version: v10.7.0
Global ESLint version: v10.7.0
Operating System: Window 11


### What parser are you using?

Default (Espree)

### What did you do?

<details>
<summary>Configuration</summary>

```js
export default [
    {
        files: ["**/*.js"],
        languageOptions: { ecmaVersion: 'lastest', sourceType: "module" },
        rules: { "no-var": "error" }
    }
];
```
</details>

```js
function f() {
    try {
        throw new Error("boom");
    } catch (e) {
        var e = e || new Error("unknown");
        console.log(e.message);
    }
}
f();
```
Running `npx eslint --fix c.js`.

### What did you expect to happen?

The declaration should not be autofixed. Per the spec, a `var` may
redeclare a catch clause parameter (B.3.4), but a `let` with the same
name is a SyntaxError. This is the same category as #11830 (`var let;`),
where autofix was disabled because the result would not parse.

### What actually happened?

The declaration was autofixed to `let`:

```js
    } catch (e) {
        let e = e || new Error("unknown");
```

Before the fix, the code runs and prints `boom`. After the fix, it does
not parse at all:

SyntaxError: Identifier 'e' has already been declared

Notably, ESLint itself reports a parsing error on its own output when
running `--fix`:

5:13 error Parsing error: Identifier 'e' has already been declared

Since this is a parse failure rather than a runtime change, the entire
script fails to load, taking any other code in the same file with it.

### Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

https://eslint.org/play/#

### Participation

- [x] I am willing to submit a pull request for this issue.

### AI acknowledgment

- [ ] I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
- [x] (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

### Additional comments

`isRedeclared` checks `variable.defs.length >= 2`, but the catch
parameter and the `var` resolve to separate variables in the scope
analysis, so the redeclaration is not detected. The equivalent case with
a *function* parameter is handled correctly and is not autofixed:

```js
function f(e) { var e = e || "fallback"; }  // correctly not fixed
function f() { try {} catch (e) { var e = e || "fallback"; } }  // fixed -> SyntaxError
```

This pattern (`catch (e) { var e = e || ... }`) shows up in older
cross-browser error handling code, so it can surface when running
`--fix` over a legacy codebase.

I am willing to submit a pull request to fix this.

title: Bug: `no-var` autofix produces a SyntaxError when a `var` redeclares the catch clause parameter
